description: id-shape (ADR 0031, ADR 0035): every id the platform mints is a ULID — 48 bits of milliseconds, 80 bits of randomness, Crockford base32, 26 characters, so ids sort in the order they were minted and no letter is misread aloud. `pattern` is the whole of the agreement, and it is a shape, not an ordering: a tier holding an id to it is saying the id will parse, not that it was minted by a clock the other tier trusts. The app mints almost all of them in production (packages/schema/src/ulid.ts) and the worker mints one: the nightly parser audit is self-scheduled, so the worker names that job itself (apps/worker/src/better_answers_worker/ids.py, T-057), and every other row it writes is a row the app already keyed. A **derived** id is not a minted one and this pattern does not reach it: a chunk's id is its document and its ordinal joined, cocoindex's stable id in ADR 0036's sense, so either tier can compute it from the address rather than being told it (contracts/document-chunk/cases.json). The two are kept apart on purpose — this shape must refuse a derived id, the way it refuses every other composed key below. `must_parse` are ids either tier may hand the other, and `must_not_parse` are the shapes this replaced, each with the reason it is refused. The TypeScript half runs the samples through its own boundary schema and mints a hundred ids the pattern must accept (packages/core/test/tier-contract.test.ts); the Python half compiles the pattern and does the same with the helper its factories seed with (apps/worker/tests/test_tier_contract.py). Neither writes the pattern out itself.

must_not_parse.why: lower case; Crockford base32 is written upper
I is excluded, so it is never confused with 1
L is excluded, so it is never confused with 1
O is excluded, so it is never confused with 0
U is excluded, so no id spells an accident
a key composed from the ids it joins; the platform mints, never composes
the identity library's own default id: mixed case, 32 characters, no time
a UUID: hyphens, lower case, and no order that matches its timestamps
